Deutetrabenazine is a deuterated from of tetrabenazine
Deuteration is a process in which the stable isotope deuterium
replaces selected hydrogen atoms, resulting in a compound with
similar pharmacodynamic effects but different pharmacokinetic
profiles, because the carbon–deuterium covalent bond requires 8
times more energy to break than a carbon–hydrogen bond
Substitution of deuterium for hydrogen slows the breakdown of
metabolites; thus, the active metabolites of deutetrabenazine have
longer half-lives and greater absorption than those of tetrabenazine
